### Carrying Jesus Into the World
Author: Izabella McMillon
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement/encouragement-for-today-october-15-2019.html
Passage: Psalm 115:1
Points:
- Corrie ten Boom likened her public ministry to the donkey that carried Jesus, knowing all acclaim belonged solely to Christ.
- Believers are called to humbly carry Jesus into the world without seeking personal recognition.
- Remembering God's surprising faithfulness in difficult seasons encourages deeper trust in His leading.
- Christians should consistently redirect attention and glory back to God's love and saving grace.

### When You Make Idols, You End Up Like Them
Author: Rick Warren
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-hope-with-rick-warren/daily-hope-with-rick-warren-june-10-2024.html
Passage: Psalm 115:8
Points:
- Looking to anything other than God for total fulfillment produces deep disillusionment and eventual spiritual bondage.
- Good things like family, achievements, or ministry become idols when treated as ultimate sources of worth.
- A person inevitably takes on the characteristics of whatever they value most in life.
- People create idols out of a desire to manage and control a god rather than submitting to Him.
- Relinquishing control and placing God first brings genuine spiritual freedom and lasting fulfillment.

### The Surprising Truth about Idols
Author: Greg Laurie
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/harvestdaily/the-surprising-truth-about-idols-greg-laurie-daily-devotion-april-15-2016.html
Passage: Psalm 115:4
Points:
- Modern idolatry rarely involves carved statues but frequently appears as obsessive admiration of famous individuals.
- Christians are vulnerable to making idols out of respected pastors or leaders whom God has used.
- Placing people on pedestals guarantees disappointment because every human being will eventually fall short.
- People naturally reflect the characteristics of whatever or whoever they worship.
- Believers must reserve their worship and trust for God alone rather than elevating created beings.

### Wisdom from the Psalms 9/14
Author: Wisdom from the Psalms
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/wisdom/wisdom-from-the-psalms-9-or-14-552570.html
Passage: Psalm 115:16
Points:
- God granting the earth to mankind is a mandate for stewardship, not license to abuse creation.
- Treating the physical world carelessly like a disposable toy risks causing lasting harm.
- Christians honor the Creator by handling His handiwork with the same care and value He demonstrates.
- Faithful stewardship of earthly gifts reflects the character needed to share in God's eternal kingdom.
